lines.en: : So, let me get this straight — you had a threesome with Imani and Rika, grabbed your pants out of the dryer, and then immediately sprinted over to me.
: I’d say it was more of a brisk jog, but yeah. That pretty much sums it up.
: Right, cool. Got it. Can I ask you a question, though?
: Sure.
: Why?
: Would you believe me if I said that being with two attractive women at once is what made me ultimately realize I only have eyes for you?
: Sure, yeah. If I was like ten years younger and you weren’t already acutely aware that I’m only interested in women. Go home.
: I can’t.
: Why? Because there’s another girl who wants to sleep with you there? And you must now use my dojo as some sort of sanctuary from sex?
: Well, when you put it that way, I am more safe here. You can be my bodyguard.
: And no, I am not ashamed to say that as I am a good guy who can formally acknowledge that sometimes girls are stronger than boys. Praise me for my political correctness.
: Weren’t you trying to find some sort of heterosexual loophole to finger me less than twenty four hours ago?
: I’d say I was just trying to learn more about your ways of life.
: Just leave! I don’t want to tell you any more about my ways of life!
: I just don’t really know what I’m supposed to do.
: I just told you what you’re supposed to do!
: No, about what they were trying to get out of me at the bar last night.
: Oh, are we being serious again? It’s hard to pick up your tone sometimes with you always muttering everything.
: Do you think it’s safe to, like...tell them? Or maybe just Imani at least?
: Do I think it’s safe for you to tell the teacher of a group of young girls that you are actively having sex with like half of them? No, Akira. I don’t think that is safe. For I am not an idiot.
: But...this is Imani we’re talking about. And you guys are like peanut butter and chocolate, so I’m sure she’d probably figure out some way to justify it and not disown you.
: Which one of us is peanut butter and which one of us is chocolate?
: What does that look imply? I am too politically correct to understand.
: Akira, I can’t tell you whether or not it’s a good idea to burden anyone else with the information you have bestowed unto me. So if that’s the advice you’re looking for, scram. I can’t help.
: It’s honestly miraculous those two haven’t already figured it out. Especially with what Rika’s daughter’s apparently been texting you.
: I mean, they kind of have. They just don’t have any sort of smoking gun to prove it yet and I’m like one step away from just handing it to them so they can shoot me.
: And do you want to get shot?
: Metaphorically. Do not use this opportunity to joke about killing yourself again.
: I don’t know. Sometimes, I don’t. Sometimes I do. And that question alone has been compelling me to do a lot of really stupid shit lately.
: You mean like fucking your girlfriend’s little sister while you’re all on a trip together and then just hoping they don’t find you?
: That’s a very specific example, Osako. Are you speaking from experience? Does Wakana have a little sister I don’t know about?
: No, you fucking moron! I’m talking about your fucking idol ex-girlfriend and how she caught you screwing her fucking sister! Come on!
: Wha- but how do you know about that?
: Because I went to a bar!
: And the whole bar was talking about it?
: No, she was! Niki!
: To the whole bar?
: Akira, I’m going to kill you one day.
: What, just to you then? What sort of coincidence is that? You guys don’t even know each other, right?
: We do now. So much so that we created a new martial art just to get back at you.
: How...was she doing? Apart from just being mad at me, which is perfectly reasonable.
: Uhh...about as good as one could expect to be after finding out their boyfriend was boning their teenage sister?
: So...bad?
: Yes, Akira. Bad. That is not a thing normal people do. So when normal-ish people like Niki Nakayama bear witness to it, they become emotional. This is called “being a human.”
: Okay, Osako. I feel bad enough about what happened. I don’t need the sarcasm.
: Do you feel bad, Akira? Or are you only just saying that because you were caught?
: No, see, I wanted to get caught. That’s how much I love her.
: Was that a joke? What was the punchline?
: Hah...It wasn’t a joke. She’s just given up her entire life for me since we were kids and she’s going to keep doing that so long as I’m in the picture.
: Just look at how much she was able to accomplish the first time we split up. She became a world famous idol. That’s what she’s capable of without me.
: Listen, I’m not going to stand here and pretend to know what sort of weird, fucked up relationship you guys have. But if you saw her now, you might be rethinking that, Akira.
: What does it matter how much a person can accomplish if they’re miserable while doing it?
: On an individual level, not much. But think of how much good she’s doing for the people out there who need her. The ones she inspires and motivates. Who revere her work and look up to her.
: Okay. I’m thinking about them. Now what? Do we just sacrifice her feelings in exchange for theirs? Does that make this okay?
: None of it’s okay. It sucks. All of it sucks. And I’m the one who is perpetuating this suckiness because I can’t bring myself to change and just keep pulling more people under with me.
: And now you think Imani and Rika will be the next to drown.
: Right. And while the answer of “don’t drown them” is most certainly the correct one, I keep telling myself it’s not. So I need you to slap some sense into-
: Did that help?
: No.
: Okay. Let me try again.
: Please don’t. Just tell me I’m an idiot and remind me of how much of a shitty situation I put you in by telling you.
: Do I not do that enough already? I feel like I remind you a lot.
: You do. My mind just can’t comprehend receiving what it wants. So even when my desires are satisfied, there’s still some sort of ingrained desire to keep going after them.
: I’m pretty sure they call that “addiction” in the real world.
: Yeah, well, the real world sounds pretty nice right about now.
: Then fucking come back down to it, asshole.
: Easier said than done, Osako.
: Easier said than done...
: Stop acting like some kind of drama protagonist by meekly repeating lines like that and just fucking do it, man.
: You’re your own worst enemy here. And it’s starting to rub off on others too. Even Ayane’s been fucking miserable lately and that girl’s always been a ray of sunshine.
: How so? What’s she doing? Is she-
: Outside. I just realized you’re not going away and I don’t want to be stuck here for the rest of the day.
: So she’s just barely showing up now? And when she does, she seems out of it?
: Yeah, that’s a good way to sum it up without having to waste like ten paragraphs on it. So did something, like...happen or?...
: Uhh...a lot has happened. It’s just kind of difficult saying what since we sort of...don’t really know.
: Well, whatever it is, that’s the same look I’ve been getting from her. And on you, it works. Fits you as a person better. It’s weird for Ayane, though. So I humbly ask you to make it stop.
: I would if I could. But just like how it is with Niki, the more involved I get, the more painful I think it will be for her.
: Ayane doesn’t normally talk about what’s bothering her. She’s the type to just hide it until she breaks into a million pieces.
: I know. Which is why this time is weird. Because either she’s given up on hiding it, or it’s just so powerful that she can’t.
: Either way, that’s something you’re more suited to deal with than me.
: I don’t know if that’s true, Osako. You probably play a bigger role in her life than I think you really understand.
: What? How?
: Well, she doesn’t have a mom. And the closest thing she does have to one already belongs to someone else, so she likely feels like a burden talking to her about anything.
: Okay. And?
: And you’re a cool, older woman who knows her and teaches her about things.
: I teach her self-defense. That’s not even remotely similar to motherhood.
: I mean...it kind of is, isn’t it? Just in the physical department instead of the mental one. I bet Ayane would be really happy if you tried getting closer to her.
: Yeah, I don’t buy it. I’m just her teacher at the end of the day. And I imagine that’s all she sees me as too.
: I mean, I am also her teacher. And I sleep with her.
: Cool, yeah. I’ll put sleeping with Ayane on my to-do list then. I’m sure that will magically cure all of her problems and definitely won’t just cause more damage in the long run.
: Wouldn’t hurt to try, would it?
: Sleeping with a high-schooler?! How did you manage to pivot from guilt to propaganda in less than thirty minutes?!
: No, obviously not sleeping with her. Just...being the cool older woman she can talk to about stuff. Stuff she won’t tell me because she knows how I am.
: How would that even work, though?
: I really only see her during lessons. And every time I’ve tried to pull her aside to ask if everything’s okay, she just says she’s fine and that she needs to go do her homework.
: Oh, easy. Just corner her.
: A statement that threatening requires a little more hesitation, don’t you think?
: Sure, but we’ve already discerned that I don’t operate on the same level as regular people. I’m the guy you come to for unconventional advice.
: Didn’t you come to me? How’d this devolve into a crash course on the steps I should take to look out for a girl who only loosely appreciates my existence?
: That’s easy, too. You’re emotionally vulnerable and I have a precedented pattern of utilizing such things to distract from my inadequacies, capitalizing on weakness for personal gain.
: You really are the product of her existence, aren’t you? The fucking abuse-poet lady. Because she was doing the same thing to you. Using you for her own personal gain.
: But that doesn’t mean she didn’t love me.
: Akira...come on.
: What? Do you think I don’t love Ayane? That that’s what I’m doing with her?
: Stop asking me to interpret all these fucked up relationships and just realize that I’m normal. Of course I’m not going to understand the perspective of someone who went through this.
: I just think that there’s a lot more...complexity regarding relationships that extend through different age groups than you do.
: And that, if I am going to talk to Ayane, that I probably shouldn’t be taking advice from a guy who’d just whip his dick out and try to cure her with that.
: You’ll actually do it then?
: I don’t know...it still feels kind of weird.
: I don’t think I’m really cut out for, like...motherly stuff if that’s the role I’m supposed to be filling right now. And I imagine she’d feel the same way.
: I think you’d be a good mom, Osako.
: Yeah, because you know all about proper parenthood, Boy.
: Maybe I don’t, but...
: I feel like I do...
: And I feel like I’m overstepping and will just make her uncomfortable.
: Only one way to find out.
: If you’re uncomfortable with it, though-
: That’s not it. It’s just...
: Sometimes, you spend so much time telling yourself what you are and what you’ll do with your life that anything outside of that vision seems sort of...I don’t know. Impossible? Foreign, maybe?
: Yeah...I think I get what you mean.
: I don’t know. Maybe I will. Maybe I won’t. I just hope she gets better soon.
: And I hope you figure out a way to confront your issues with other adults instead of leeching off of my lesbian wisdom all the time.
: It is not my fault that lesbians are so wise. Do you blame Harry Potter for going to Gandalf for advice in Star Wars?
: You have no idea what you just said, do you?
: I say a lot of things, Osako. I can’t be expected to know all of them.
: Seriously. Just go home.
I accompany Osako back to her apartment (against her will) and spend the rest of the trek home deciding what I want to do with Imani and Rika.
Besides having more sex with them, I mean.
And what I land on is this-
No matter what happens, it can only be good.
For I want to be caught, but I don’t.
And I want to be loved, but I don’t.
I want to be fixed.
I don’t.

Imani’s affection has increased to [imani_love]!
Imani’s lust has increased to [imani_lust]!
